ratingBasis: preseason July-2025 W², spreads via the fitted spread head
caveat: Proof-of-concept on 2025 using static preseason ratings — the market sharpens week to week, so late-season edges partly reflect projection staleness, not just pricing. The robust biases (margin cap, home field, conference) are the real, exploitable vulnerabilities. 2026 fills in weekly.
insights: Across 762 games, the W² line missed the final margin by 13.79 pts on average vs the market's 11.84. W² was the closer number in 40.2% of games.
Betting every game where W² disagreed with the close by 3+ pts went 252–263 ATS (48.9%, -6.6% ROI at -110) — the model got picked off on its disagreements. (Break-even is 52.4%.)
Biggest conference bias: W² underrated FBS Independents by 4.02 pts/game (23 team-games) — fade them against the number.

On blowout lines (21+), W² still priced the favorite 9.9 pts below the market (post-calibration) across 109 games. Tested: raising the margin cap does NOT fix this — the residual is preseason projection error (we didn't know the elites would be THIS good), not the cap. Keep the cap at 28 for clean strength.
tuning: Conference strength: FBS Independents ran -4.02 — its members' regression target looks miscalibrated.
Blowouts: the residual is projection error, not the cap (experiment_cap.py confirms looser caps don't help). The real lever is in-season rating updates, not a preseason knob.
